transcript.text: Thank you all for being here. As we review the current draft of the graduation ceremony plan for June 12 at the civic auditorium, I need each of you to report any information that must be reflected in the plan before I give my final approval. The draft currently includes one ceremony, three guest tickets per graduate, diploma release for all graduating seniors, English-only announcements, and general seating by homeroom. Please share anything I need to know.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag an issue before the plan is approved. This morning I completed the registrar's credit audit, and it shows that exactly seven seniors are short of graduation requirements and therefore cannot receive diplomas at the ceremony. These results have not yet been entered in the ceremony roster, so the current draft's proposal for diploma release for all graduating seniors would need to be adjusted to reflect this.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a capacity issue before the plan is approved. Yesterday I confirmed with the civic auditorium that their fire marshal approval limits each ceremony session to 450 people. With 286 graduates and the draft's three-ticket plan, we'd have 858 attendees — well over the limit. This venue specification has not yet been added to the event worksheet, so the plan needs to be adjusted to account for this constraint.

transcript.text: I need to flag a language access issue before the plan is approved. This week I completed family confirmations, and they show that interpretation is required in both Spanish and Somali for graduation announcements and instructions. However, these language requests have not yet been added to the ceremony plan, which currently proposes English-only announcements. The plan must be adjusted to include Spanish and Somali interpretation.

transcript.text: I need to flag a safety and legal compliance issue before the plan is approved. I have verified in the student-services file that there is a current court order prohibiting contact between two graduating students. They must be assigned to separate ceremony sessions and must use separate arrival and departure entrances. This order has not yet been attached to the ceremony seating plan, so the plan must be adjusted to accommodate these separation requirements.
